correctness.rationale: Character orthogonality converts the fourth moment exactly to the squared l2 norm of the coefficient self-convolution. Translating a three-set leaves six unordered pair sums; their possible nontrivial collisions reduce exhaustively to midpoint and double-sum equations. Cyclic torsion then yields exactly five collision patterns. Each pattern is optimized by a sharp one-variable quadratic or, for the order-three coset, the exact three-point L4/L2 inequality. Equality conditions follow from equality in the triangle and arithmetic-geometric mean steps. The checker independently enumerates all triples for N from 3 through 80 and verifies the taxonomy and extremizing witnesses.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the smallest nontrivial finite cyclic Lambda(4) problem, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It identifies exactly how 2-, 3-, and 4-torsion change the sharp fourth-moment constant, gives every extremizer, and separates generic, one-relation, and multiple-collision geometry. These exact base cases are useful for testing broader Lambda(p), additive-energy, and finite-group restriction principles.
